text:
**About 300-350 W of solar recharges a 1,000 Wh power station from empty in one good sunny day. 200 W works if you can wait about a day and a half.**

**The math**
Panel watts ≈ capacity ÷ (peak sun hours × real-world efficiency). Panels usually deliver 70-75% of their rating after heat, angle and charging losses.

- At 4.5 sun hours and 70% efficiency: 1,000 ÷ (4.5 × 0.7) ≈ **317 W** ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).
- At 4 sun hours and 75%: about **340 W**. At 5 sun hours: about 270 W ([Power Runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/)).
- In a good summer: about **300 W**. In a northern winter (about 2 sun hours): **700 W or more** ([Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)).

**Common panel sizes on an average day (4.5 sun hours)**
| Panel | Energy per day | Time to refill 1,000 Wh |
|---|---|---|
| 100 W | ~315 Wh | ~3 days |
| 200 W | ~630 Wh | ~1.5 days |
| 400 W | ~1,260 Wh | under a day |

(Figures from [Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/) and [Watt48](https://www.watt48.com/guides/solar-panel-charging-power-station).)

**Check before you buy**
- **Solar input limit:** Your station caps how many watts it accepts. Panels beyond that add nothing ([Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/how-much-solar-to-recharge)). Many 1,000 Wh units accept 400-800 W, but some accept only 200 W.
- **Voltage:** The panel's open-circuit voltage (Voc) must stay inside the station's input window. Going over can damage the station. Wiring panels in series adds voltage, so parallel is the safer default.
- **Connectors:** Check that the panel's connector or adapter matches your station.
- **Using it while charging:** Any power you draw during the day slows the recharge.

**A panel option**
If your station accepts 400 W and a 12-60 V input, the [ALLPOWERS SP037 400 W foldable panel](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-sp037-400w-solar-panel) fits. It lists at $299, or $269.10 with code ALLPOWERS26, which the page says was tested in the store's cart on 2026-10-21 and expires 2026-12-30.

- It has a Voc of 45.3 V and includes MC4→XT60 and DC adapters.
- It weighs 18.5 kg (about 41 lb), which is heavy for a folding panel.
- It's too high-voltage for stations with low input limits, such as 24-28 V max.
- The link is an affiliate link, and the store's checkout has the final word on price.
